- Token usage roll-up is reported in goal results and `/goal` output (agent runs, total/reported/estimated tokens,
  inference requests). The report marks the total as incomplete when any child task usage is unavailable. When
  `operation.policy.maxTotalTokens` is set, the driver pauses the goal at a safe boundary before starting new work
  once rolled-up child task token totals reach the cap. Missing or corrupt accounting also pauses the goal, because
  the cap cannot be enforced from a partial sum; the pause reason identifies unavailable usage. Resume continues
  after the operator repairs the record, raises or removes the cap, or cancels. This is a safe-boundary limit: one
  already-running batch can consume more than the configured cap before the next check.
- PA-3 stall counting is fingerprint-based at operation unit execution: consecutive failures with the same fingerprint count toward `policy.maxStallsPerFingerprint` (default 3), not raw turn count. A stall blocks the unit with `NOT_CONVERGING`. `retry` preserves the fingerprint count; `revise`, `replace`, `set_inputs`, `lift_context_budget`, and `assign` clear it. Operation schema v7 stores this policy/state; v6 records migrate by adding only the schema version, and older binaries refuse v7 records.
- Deterministic PA-3 acceptance is recorded in `PA3_ACCEPTANCE.md` (stale pause, token budget, fingerprint stalls, verifier-receipt gates). Restart interrupted-effect reconciliation and live-gateway qualification remain open. `/team` leaves the experimental catalogue label after PA-1 and PA-2.
- Restart-specific interrupted-effect reconciliation beyond stale-boot pause still requires qualification.
- No inference-provider or homelab-ai changes are required. Provider-neutral end-to-end qualification remains separate.

the recovery questions only; no peer code was copied. XERJ marked the corpus as incompletely indexed, so absence of a

boot-id pattern (`cli/src/upgrade_journal.ts` / `currentUpgradeBootId`) and durable operation pause semantics. A

not establish a peer pattern, so no further code was borrowed.

# Execution convergence: one lifecycle for autonomous work

Branch `fix/inference-transport-cause`, baseline 9f103ee. Code references are to `cli/src`.

```
user workflow/command (/team [experimental], nexus operation [experimental])
  -> orchestration strategy (TeamOrchestrator: roles -> work units)
  -> durable work units + dependencies (DurableOperationState, OperationStore)
  -> convergence scheduler (ConvergenceScheduler decides; OperationRunner owns time, execution, persistence)
  -> agent turn (AgentWorkUnitExecutor -> runTurn) / provider recovery (ProviderRecoveryController) / context admission
  -> tools + inference resources (ResourceRegistry, LocalLlmClient)
```
111:| PA-3 | Goal semantics: a ledger entry active from an earlier process resumes **paused** (opencode `goal.ts` boot id), stall counting by failure fingerprint and not turn count, completion decided only by a verifier receipt, an optional token budget rolling up from sub-operations (reference: Codex goal budget); `/team` leaves experimental only after PA-1 and PA-2 | stale goal resumes paused with a visible reason; a model "I am done" does not complete a goal | M | P2 (stale pause/budget + fingerprint stalls landed; deterministic acceptance recorded in PA3_ACCEPTANCE.md; `/team` experimental lift follows PA-1/PA-2) |
112:| PA-4 | **Bounded delegation and workflow commands** (trail 428; [baseline](PA4_BASELINE.md)): extend transient `spawn_subagent` and durable operations with a shared validated delegation contract/outcome, enforce authority intersection and recursive/resource limits, then expose real `/goal`, `/loop`, and `/batch` lifecycles through REPL and TUI/sidecar. # Changelog

All notable changes to Nexus Code are documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Detailed per-release documentation is maintained in [`docs/releases/`](docs/releases/).

## [Unreleased]

Inventory of work already on `release/v1.3.0` toward v1.3.0 (version strings still 1.2.2). Full unit table and open gaps: [`docs/releases/v1.3.0-READINESS.md`](docs/releases/v1.3.0-READINESS.md). External qualification pending; not a frontier-grade claim.

### Added
- Client protocol schemas and docs (PF-1), `nexus run --json` result contract (PF-2).
- ACP adapter and conformance fixtures against Zed and CodeCompanion (AC-1, AC-2).
- `nexus verify`, MCP/ACP verify surfaces, sandbox-denial receipt records (VR-1, VR-2, VR-3).
- Managed policy tiers, audit export/verify, flight hash chain, telemetry transparency and opt-out, admin strict mode and allowlists (GV-1–GV-5).
- LSP lifecycle, bounds, position encodings and project roots (LS-1, LS-2).
- Experimental detached jobs: a supervised Linux runner, isolated worktrees, unattended policy, bounded budgets, receipts, recovery, and operator commands (BG-1).
- Experimental unattended schedules (BG-2): `nexus schedule add|list|status|remove|pause|resume|run-now` with `--cron`, `--every` and `--at` (UTC); the runner starts each run as an unattended job through the same path as `nexus job start`. A schedule needs a trusted workspace, fixes its permission level when added and is a path the agent's file tools refuse; missed runs are counted and reported (an optional single catch-up job with `--on-missed run-once`, never a burst), overlapping runs are skipped and recorded, and a clock stepped backwards never runs a slot twice. The job receipt gains `schedule_occurrence` and a filled-in `missed` (additive, version 1); new schedule file schema `docs/protocol/schedule-v1.schema.json` and [`docs/SCHEDULES.md`](docs/SCHEDULES.md).
- CI CLI-suite shard fan-out under stable required check names.
- Experimental unix-socket transport for the sidecar (PF-3): `sidecar.js --listen` binds a socket (mode 0600) in a private 0700 directory and prints its path on one stdout line; other clients attach with a per-start random token from a 0600 descriptor file, as one controller or as read-only observers, and may detach and attach again. A wrong, missing or late token is refused with one fixed line before any command is parsed. No client can grant allow-always or change the mode over the socket, and `--listen` is refused under auto approval. No TCP, HTTP or WebSocket listener. Protocol stays 1 (new error codes `UNAUTHORIZED`, `NOT_CONTROLLER`, `NOT_PERMITTED`); `docs/PROTOCOL.md` "Socket transport", `examples/attach/`.
- Command hooks (HK-1): `pre-tool` and `post-tool` programs declared in `~/.config/nexus/hooks.json` or an approved `<workspace>/.nexus/hooks.json`; a hook can deny a tool call and can never approve one or change its input. Approving project hooks needs a person at a terminal and covers the workspace scripts the hooks run. `nexus hooks list|approve|revoke|test`, a `hooks.config` doctor finding, `docs/HOOKS.md`.

### Direct Shell Execution (`!`)
Run raw bash/zsh commands instantly inside the active workspace without invoking the LLM:
```text
nexus (qwen2.5-coder) my-app ❯ !git status
nexus (qwen2.5-coder) my-app ❯ !cargo check
nexus (qwen2.5-coder) my-app ❯ !npm test
```

### Slash Commands Cheatsheet

| Command | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `/help` | Display cheatsheet of all available commands |
| `/status` | View active model, endpoint, shell, git badge, context sizing with sources, last request count, objective progress |
| `/plan [add\|done\|start\|clear]` | Formulate and manage multi-phase milestone execution plan |
| `/tui` | REPL only: open the session dashboard (not offered in the live TUI, where it had no purpose) |
| `/doctor [--deep] [--fix [--yes]]` | Diagnose this session's configuration, endpoint, engine, shell and state (see `docs/DOCTOR_TROUBLESHOOTING.md`) |
| `/upgrade [--check\|--version <v>\|--yes]` | Check for updates or safely upgrade to the latest stable or pinned release with deliberate approval |

| `/theme [name]` | View or switch terminal color theme (Catppuccin, Nord, Dracula, etc.) |
| `/team <role\|full> <task>` | Orchestrate multi-agent team (Researcher, Architect, Implementer, Tester) |
| `/image <path> [prompt]` | Ingest multi-modal image / screenshot into vision model context |
| `/checkpoint [name]` | Create a safe rollback snapshot of the workspace |
| `/checkpoint diff <id>` | View file diff between current workspace and a checkpoint |
| `/checkpoint prune [keep]` | Prune older checkpoints, retaining the latest N (default: 5) |
| `/checkpoints` | List all saved workspace rollback snapshots |
| `/undo` | Roll back workspace changes to the last checkpoint |
| `/diff` | Display colored syntax-highlighted git diff |
| `/git` | Show uncommitted files and git status |
| `/commit [msg]` | Generate or execute Conventional Commit from staged changes |
| `/audit [count]` | Inspect visual tool execution audit trail (recent N entries) |
| `/compact [--llm]` | Distill earlier conversation into structured memory; queued while work runs, committed durably (archive, task state, session) |
| `/mode [auto\|review]` | Toggle autonomous execution vs human approval. Review mode asks before file changes, commands (including MCP and plugin tools) and network access; network access is asked once per destination per session |
| `/sessions` | List saved past sessions |
| `/save [name]` | Save current conversation session to `~/.nexus/sessions/` |
| `/resume [id]` | Resume an existing session |
| `/export [md\|json]` | Export session conversation transcript to a file in workspace |
| `/skills` | List discovered agent skills (`SKILL.md`) |
| `/skill [init <name>\|<name>]` | Scaffold new skill template or inspect full instructions |
| `/mcp [add\|resources\|prompts]` | Manage MCP servers, tools, resources, and prompt templates |
| `/plugins` | List loaded custom plugins and lifecycle hooks |
| `/tokens` | Display visual BPE token accounting gauge and context breakdown |
| `/onboard` | Scan workspace tech stack and generate customized `AGENTS.md` & diagram |
| `/test [filter]` | Auto-detect and run test suite with compiler diagnostic parsing |
| `/init` | Scaffold `AGENTS.md` project rules file |
| `/model [name]` | Inspect or switch active model |
| `/shell [bash\|zsh]` | Switch execution shell |
| `/cd <path>` | Switch active workspace directory |
| `/history [query\|!n]` | Fuzzy history search or re-execute item by index |
| `/copy [diff\|code\|last]` | Copy diff, code blocks, or response to system clipboard. With no clipboard tool (`wl-copy`, `xclip`, `xsel`, `pbcopy`: SSH, tmux, headless) the live TUI asks the terminal to copy it with an OSC 52 request instead (up to 74,994 bytes; larger text is refused, never cut). The terminal does not confirm it: terminals may ignore OSC 52, tmux needs `set -g set-clipboard on`, GNU screen is not supported. The text reaches the terminal only base64-encoded, after the same credential redaction and control-character handling as every sidecar message. `NEXUS_OSC52=off` (also `0`, `false`, `no`, `none`) turns the fallback off, and the older line-mode REPL does not use it. |
| `/paste` | Paste clipboard content into prompt |
| `/exit` or `/quit` | Exit session cleanly |

---

## 3. High-Efficiency Tooling Parity
25:### Fixed
26-- BG-2 schedule recovery after a crash between job submit and schedule update: restore `lastFire`, decrement `remainingRuns`, and disable at zero so `--max-runs 1` cannot fire again; treat an in-flight job for the same slot as recovery, not overlap.
27-
28-### Changed
29-- Parallel resource admission for operations (PA-1 partial); staged PA-4 workflow surfaces as documented under `docs/v1.3.0/`.
30-
31-### Not yet in Unreleased (still open on the plan)
49:### Fixed
50-- A failing type-check whose output is coloured is `FAILED`, not `ENVIRONMENT`. With `FORCE_COLOR=1` in the operator's environment `tsc` wraps the file, line and column in escape sequences; the diagnostics parser then located no file and the check was classified "could not run", which does not block completion (VC-6, CG-4). Escape sequences are removed before parsing.
51-- A native worker that exits right after launch (for example a Docker worker whose container fails to start) no longer raises an uncaught `EPIPE` that ended the CLI: the worker's stdin stream has an error listener and the waiting request is answered as a disconnect.
52-- Saving progress no longer fails on a worktree binding left over from an earlier turn ("Task state worktree path has no selected workspace identity"); it showed only when the workspace directory name tripped the secret classifier's high-entropy check.
53-- VC-6: Cargo projects are part of the pre-change type-check baseline (the per-workspace target directory is reused, so dependencies are not built twice); a regression case covers a pre-existing Rust diagnostic against a new one in an untouched caller.
617:| `/team <role\|full> <task>` | Orchestrate multi-agent team (Researcher, Architect, Implementer, Tester) |
823:- **Destructive Command Convenience Tripwire (REQ-SEC-108)**: Shell-words tokenization in TypeScript and Rust blocks obviously destructive commands (`rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, raw block device writes, fork bombs) without false positives on legitimate project commands (`rm -rf ./build`, `rm -rf /tmp/x`, `grep reboot`, `echo shutdown`, `chown -R me /srv`). This denylist is a **convenience tripwire** to catch obvious mistakes, **not a security boundary**. Known bypasses (such as `find / -delete`, `/bin/rm -rf /`, `rm -r -f /`, Python scripts) are documented non-goals that pass by design; the sandbox (`--sandbox`) and approval posture (`review`) form the security boundary.

| Cause | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| process gone | the recorded pid is not running |
| pid recycled | the pid is alive but its start time differs: another process holds it now |
| other host | the record names a different host; its processes cannot be checked from here |
| other boot | the boot id differs: the host rebooted |
| identity unknown | a field is missing, malformed or unverifiable (a record from before `activeStartTicks`, a hand edit, a platform without `/proc`) |

The same rule (`core/driver_identity.ts`) runs on the read path (`/goal status|list|show`, `nexus operation status`, `--dag`, which show `PAUSED` and the reason without writing anything) and on the drive path (`driveOperation` persists the pause and runs no unit). The only exemption is a plan that no one ever started: no identity at all, every unit waiting with zero runs. An operation `BLOCKED` at an operator decision stays at that decision. When the operator applies a decision, the command records its own process as the new driver before resuming; a later death of that process is detected.

Compatibility: the state schema stays at v7. `activeStartTicks` is an optional additive field; a record written by the previous build has none and reads as unknown identity, so an interrupted goal from an older build pauses once and resumes after the operator's explicit resume. This pause, not the lock, is what stops a second run: the driver lock (`<id>.lock`, which holds its own start ticks) separately keeps two live processes from driving one operation, and a read-only command run while another process drives reports "Driven by pid N" instead of failing with the lock error. Identity comes from `/proc`, so on a platform without it an interrupted goal always pauses.
